questions.stem:
The number of hours spent exercising each week by a group of students is shown in the following table.

| **Exercising time** (**in hours**) | **Number of students** |
|:---:|:---:|
| $2$ | $5$ |
| $3$ | $1$ |
| $4$ | $4$ |
| $5$ | $3$ |
| $6$ | $x$ |

The median is $4.5$ hours.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
**EITHER**

recognising that half the total frequency is $10$ (may be seen in an ordered list or indicated on the frequency table) ***(A1)***

**OR**

$5 + 1 + 4 = 3 + x$ ***(A1)***

**OR**

$\sum f = 20$ ***(A1)***

**THEN**

$x = 7$ ***A1***

questions.stem:
A company is designing a new logo. The logo is created by removing two equal segments from a rectangle, as shown in the following diagram.

**diagram not to scale**

![The logo: a rectangle with a curved segment removed from each of the two longer sides.](content/papers/img/2022-may-p2-tz1-q3-logo.png)

The rectangle measures $5\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$. The points A and B lie on a circle, with centre O and radius $2\text{ cm}$, such that $\text{A}\hat{\text{O}}\text{B} = \theta$, where $0 < \theta < \pi$. This information is shown in the following diagram.

**diagram not to scale**

![Rectangle 4 wide and 5 high. On the left side, O lies outside the rectangle; OA = 2, angle AOB = θ, and the shaded segment between chord AB and the arc lies inside the rectangle. An equal shaded segment is on the right side.](content/papers/img/2022-may-p2-tz1-q3-diagram.png)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of one of the shaded segments in terms of $\theta$.
parts.markscheme:
valid approach to find area of segment by finding area of sector $-$ area of triangle ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta - \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta$

$\dfrac{1}{2}(2)^2\theta - \dfrac{1}{2}(2)^2\sin\theta$ ***(A1)***

area $= 2\theta - 2\sin\theta$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the area of the logo is $13.4\text{ cm}^2$, find the value of $\theta$.
parts.markscheme:
**EITHER**

area of logo $=$ area of rectangle $-$ area of segments ***(M1)***

$5 \times 4 - 2 \times (2\theta - 2\sin\theta) = 13.4$ ***(A1)***

**OR**

area of one segment $= \dfrac{20 - 13.4}{2} \ (= 3.3)$ ***(M1)***

$2\theta - 2\sin\theta = 3.3$ ***(A1)***

**THEN**

$\theta = 2.35672\ldots$

$\theta = 2.36$ (do not accept an answer in degrees) ***A1***

> **Note:** Award ***(M1)(A1)A0*** if there is more than one solution.  
> Award ***(M1)(A1FT)A0*** if the candidate works in degrees and obtains a final answer of $135.030\ldots$

questions.stem:
**All lengths in this question are in centimetres.**

A solid metal ornament is in the shape of a right pyramid, with vertex V and square base ABCD. The centre of the base is X. Point V has coordinates $(1,\ 5,\ 0)$ and point A has coordinates $(-1,\ 1,\ 6)$.

**diagram not to scale**

![Right pyramid with vertex V above the centre X of the square base ABCD.](content/papers/img/2022-may-p2-tz1-q7.png)

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
attempt to use the distance formula to find $\text{AV}$ ***(M1)***

$\sqrt{(1 - (-1))^2 + (5 - 1)^2 + (0 - 6)^2}$

$= 7.48331\ldots$

$= 7.48$ (cm) $\left(= \sqrt{56} \text{ or } 2\sqrt{14}\right)$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1**

attempt to apply cosine rule OR sine rule to find $\text{AB}$ ***(M1)***

$(\text{AB} =)\ \sqrt{7.48\ldots^2 + 7.48\ldots^2 - 2 \times 7.48\ldots \times 7.48\ldots \cos(40^\circ)}$ OR $\dfrac{\text{AB}}{\sin 40^\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{56}}{\sin 70^\circ}$ ***(A1)***

$= 5.11888\ldots$

$= 5.12$ (cm) ***A1***

**METHOD 2**

Let M be the midpoint of $[\text{AB}]$

attempt to apply right-angled trigonometry on triangle AVM ***(M1)***

$= 2 \times 7.48\ldots \times \sin(20^\circ)$ ***(A1)***

$= 5.11888\ldots$

$= 5.12$ (cm) ***A1***

parts.label: c
parts.intro: The volume of the pyramid is $57.2\text{ cm}^3$, correct to three significant figures.
parts.text: Find the height of the pyramid, $\text{VX}$.
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1**

equating volume of pyramid formula to $57.2$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{1}{3} \times 5.11\ldots^2 \times h = 57.2$ ***(A1)***

$h = 6.54886\ldots$

$h = 6.55$ (cm) ***A1***

**METHOD 2**

Let M be the midpoint of $[\text{AB}]$

$\text{AV}^2 = \text{AM}^2 + \text{MX}^2 + \text{XV}^2$ ***(M1)***

$$\Rightarrow \text{XV} = \sqrt{7.48\ldots^2 - \left(\dfrac{5.11\ldots}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\dfrac{5.11\ldots}{2}\right)^2}$$ ***(A1)***

$h = 6.54886\ldots$

$h = 6.55$ (cm) ***A1***

parts.label: d
parts.intro: A second ornament is in the shape of a cuboid with a rectangular base of length $2x\text{ cm}$, width $x\text{ cm}$ and height $y\text{ cm}$. The cuboid has the same volume as the pyramid.
parts.text: The cuboid has a minimum surface area of $S\text{ cm}^2$. Find the value of $S$.
parts.markscheme:
$V = x \times 2x \times y = 57.2$ ***(A1)***

$S = 2\left(2x^2 + xy + 2xy\right)$ ***A1***

> **Note:** Condone use of $A$.

attempt to substitute $y = \dfrac{57.2}{2x^2}$ into their expression for surface area ***(M1)***

$(S(x) =)\ 4x^2 + 6x\left(\dfrac{57.2}{2x^2}\right)$

**EITHER**

attempt to find minimum turning point on graph of area function ***(M1)***

**OR**

$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}S}{\mathrm{d}x} = 8x - 171.6x^{-2} = 0$ OR $x = 2.77849\ldots$ ***(M1)***

**THEN**

$92.6401\ldots$

minimum surface area $= 92.6$ (cm$^2$) ***A1***

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{4x + 1}{x + 4}$, where $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $x \neq -4$.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
(i) $x = -4$ ***A1***

(ii) attempt to substitute into $y = \dfrac{a}{c}$ OR table with large values of $x$ OR sketch of $f$ showing asymptotic behaviour ***(M1)***

$y = 4$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(i) Find $f^{-1}(x)$.

(ii) Using an algebraic approach, show that the graph of $f^{-1}$ is obtained by a reflection of the graph of $f$ in the $y$-axis followed by a reflection in the $x$-axis.
parts.markscheme:
(i) $y = \dfrac{4x + 1}{x + 4}$

attempt to interchange $x$ and $y$ (seen anywhere) ***M1***

$xy + 4y = 4x + 1$ OR $xy + 4x = 4y + 1$ ***(A1)***

$xy - 4x = 1 - 4y$ OR $xy - 4y = 1 - 4x$ ***(A1)***

$f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1 - 4x}{x - 4}$ $\left(\text{accept } y = \dfrac{1 - 4x}{x - 4}\right)$ ***A1***

(ii) reflection in $y$-axis given by $f(-x)$ ***(M1)***

$f(-x) = \dfrac{-4x + 1}{-x + 4}$ ***(A1)***

reflection of their $f(-x)$ in $x$-axis given by $-f(-x)$ accept “now $-f(x)$” ***M1***

$\left(-f(-x) =\right)\ -\dfrac{-4x + 1}{-x + 4}$

$= \dfrac{-4x + 1}{x - 4}$ OR $\dfrac{4x - 1}{-x + 4}$ ***A1***

$= \dfrac{1 - 4x}{x - 4} \ \left(= f^{-1}(x)\right)$ ***AG***

> **Note:** If the candidate attempts to show the result using a particular coordinate on the graph of $f$ rather than a general coordinate on the graph of $f$, where appropriate, award marks as follows:  
> ***M0A0*** for eg $(2,\ 3) \to (-2,\ 3)$  
> ***M0A0*** for $(-2,\ 3) \to (-2,\ -3)$

parts.label: c
parts.intro: The graphs of $f$ and $f^{-1}$ intersect at $x = p$ and $x = q$, where $p < q$.
parts.text:
(i) Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.

(ii) Hence, find the area enclosed by the graph of $f$ and the graph of $f^{-1}$.
parts.markscheme:
(i) attempt to solve $f(x) = f^{-1}(x)$ using graph or algebraically ***(M1)***

$p = -1$ AND $q = 1$ ***A1***

> **Note:** Award ***(M1)A0*** if only one correct value seen.

(ii) attempt to set up an integral to find area between $f$ and $f^{-1}$ ***(M1)***

$$\int_{-1}^{1} \left(\dfrac{4x + 1}{x + 4} - \dfrac{1 - 4x}{x - 4}\right) \mathrm{d}x$$ ***(A1)***

$= 0.675231\ldots$

$= 0.675$ ***A1***
